content: My colleagues and I are a group of grad students and faculty from the University of Nebraska--Lincoln planning on attempting to formalize max flow/min cut in Lean this summer and are open to any thoughts/guidance that people have for us. We are aware of the recent attempt #34028.

Hello!

Reese White said:

any thoughts/guidance that people have for us

Since you cited the mathlib PR I assume the plan is to merge it into mathlib rather than a personal project, so my advice would be to start PRing small bits as soon as possible. e.g. add some lemmas that you expect you'll need, and define cuts and flows.

Can you share roughly how you'd like to define flows?
This effort in Isabelle is something to be aware of, it might contain some relevant ideas that transfer to the dependently typed context: https://github.com/mabdula/Isabelle-Graph-Library
Another relevant effort. #CSLib: Code Reasoning > Example of Max-flow Min-cut Theorem in Lean

Thanks for the references! (I'm someone else on the UNL team.) The one @Shreyas Srinivas linked seems particularly relevant, in fact, our initial look makes it seem like a completely finished implementation!

@Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai , are there any plans to merge this into CSLib (or into MathLib)? Is there anything that would be helpful for us to contribute towards that?
(Sorry for the @ here, I seem to be unable to respond to your original message.)

Dear Anna, thank you for the message. Yes, definitely, graph algorithms are welcome to cslib. Currently, I (with my working group) am developing a downstream graph algorithm repo that will be upstreamed to cslib. I think porting the max-flow min-cut theorem from there to our new graph definition would be very helpful.
